NAZA (15)

Fri 16 Oct —Wed 18 Nov 2026 ,Cinemas

Cloaked in darkness on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, Israeli journalist Yuval Abraham conducts shattering one-on-one interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence personnel.

This urgent piece of documentary investigation by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is a deep dive into the systems and technologies underpinning Israel’s bombing campaign in Gaza. 

The title Naza refers to a military intelligence acronym used to indicate the number of civilians expected to be killed in an airstrike.

Following their Oscar-winning film No Other Land, Abraham and Szor turn their attention to how these systems of remote surveillance and mass killing operate, seeking to grasp the horrific scale of civilian deaths.

Both Israeli filmmakers have now been denounced as traitors in Israel, and the Israeli Prime Minister has personally threatened to revoke their citizenship. The film premiered (and won the Special Jury Prize) at the Venice Film Festival. 

Tagged with: Cinema Magic Mondays New releases

Content Consideration: Distressing footage depicts partial sight of the dead bodies of children and young people buried under rubble following a bombing in Gaza, Palestine.

The British Board of Film Classification (BBFC) provides guidance to audiences, to help them choose what’s right for them and avoid what’s not. For guidance, please click here and type the film title into the search bar.

Location
Barbican Cinema 1 is located within the main Barbican building on Level -2. Head to Level G and walk towards the Lakeside Terrace where you’ll find stairs and lifts to take you down to the venue floor.

Public transport
The Barbican is widely accessible by bus, tube, train and by foot or bicycle. Plan your journey and find more route information in ‘Your Visit’ or book your car parking space in advance.

Location
Barbican Cinema 2 & 3 are located on Beech Street, a short walk from the Barbican’s Silk Street entrance. From Silk Street, you’ll see a zebra crossing that will take you over the road to the venue. 

Address
Beech Street, London
EC2Y 8DS

Nearby public transport
We are within walking distance from a number of London Underground stations, the closest being Barbican, St Paul’s and Moorgate. The nearest train stations are Liverpool Street and Farringdon. Bus Route 153 runs directly past the Barbican along Chiswell Street
